chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: CBS staff job and shows
summary: After the Hodges group he joined CBS staff around 1956, playing radio and television shows including Gleason, Patti Page and Sullivan.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: All right, getting back to New York, after you left Johnny's group, was that at the time it broke up? Or --
Yes, it had just about broken up when I got out.
And then was when you start -- went into studio work in New York. Is that right?
Oh, yes. I had been over to the studios and finally got a call. CBS come -- there was a vacancy, I remember, on staff, and I got the job.
And that was what year?
I think that was '56.
And so at CBS, when you went on staff, Warren Covington was the one who (inaudible) left.
Warren, yes, Warren.
-- here in Stanley's book. And what kind of shows were you playing on? What kind of music were you playing?
All kinds. We played radio, played the TV, played any show, any assignment that the -- that the studio turned over to you.
Specifically can you remember what some of the shows you played? of them were?
Oh, was the Jackie Gleason Shows, the Patti Page, the Sunday Night Big Man show, Sullivan, and oh, innumerable shows. You just went on anything you --
(End of proceedings as recorded.)

You were saying that you
-- to play the Ed Sullivan show with CBS and what else?
Any -- any show that -- that the office wanted you to fit in. And so, you'd get the schedule which meant next day show up at such and such a time, and play such and such a show, radio, T.V, anything.
Were you playing only at CBS at that time, or did you do any other work? Did you make any personal appearances, do any --
No. I did several recordings, but no, we didn't do too much outside of work because it would conflict with the schedule because you never knew when you had to go to work on this -- these other shows.
Musical Physical
Did you enjoy working there? Physically did you enjoy it?

Musically it was beautiful, but it's kind of nerve wracking. You see, everything that goes into T.V. or radio is recorded for the studio. And so, it would record your mistakes also which made you very nervous. And it was pretty tight.
But it was beautiful how?
Well, the men were beautiful, good musicians. Could play any kind of music. And it -- I consider that the tops in music. I never will forget the time

that the leader -- the big leader in the show I was working with was Ray Block. And there was one time when the symphony -- not symphony, the opera group had a show there. And I don't think Ray had ever tried to direct the opera -- an opera.

So, we had this rehearsal this morning, and then the show goes on a little later. And it was perfect. Those are the kind of men, you know. Everybody was delighted with the way the band went of, as if we had been playing opera for years. And it's very gratifying to be a part of that kind of an organization.
